subject: AuroraFin security kickoff — questionnaire start & action items
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <e.cruz@aurorafin.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: security kickoff & questionnaire initiation

Hi Elena — thanks for the call today, great to meet the AuroraFin team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the security path to contract: 

Key notes from today:
- AuroraFin is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing summarization features (low-risk PII flow described on call).
- Procurement timeline: internal approvals expected by end of Nov; target pilot Jan.

Security asks you flagged we should start with:
1) SOC 2: you asked whether we have a Type II report and whether a summary/bridge letter is available.
2) Data residency & GDPR: you mentioned EU residency for a subset of customers; need clarity on region controls.
3) HIPAA/BAA: AuroraFin will need confirmation on HIPAA posture and BAA support.
4) Questionnaire form: you preferred CAIQ as a fast path but are open to SIG or our custom form depending on evidence.
5) KMS/BYOK & encryption at rest: you want to confirm whether customer-managed keys are supported.

Proposed next actions (can we confirm these?):
- AuroraFin: fill the attached scope spreadsheet (aurorafin_sig_scope.xlsx) with hosting/tenant/residency preferences and evidence owners — deadline Nov 12.
- Redwood: Grace/Kimberly will kick off a CAIQ prefill and prepare our SOC 2 summary and encryption/KMS spec. We’ll post a shared Drive folder and invite your security contact.
- Schedule a 30-minute prefill call (security-to-security) next week to run through ambiguous fields and agree what evidence to exchange.

Please confirm owners for evidence (SOC 2, network diagrams, app architecture) and whether procurement needs any specific doc for early review. I’ll follow up with calendar invites and a Drive link.

Thanks — Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Cruz <e.cruz@aurorafin.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraFin Security Team <security@aurorafin.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T18:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: security kickoff & questionnaire initiation

Thanks Jordan — short answers below and attached is our scope matrix (see aurorafin_sig_scope.xlsx).

- SOC 2: We require a current SOC 2 Type II for vendors; if you have a recent report or summary we can accept that for initial review. A full report will be required before production.
- Data residency: We operate both US and EU customers. Pilot will use US residency, but production requires the option for EU residency (data-at-rest in eu-west).
- HIPAA: Yes — AuroraFin handles PHI for a subset of customers. BAA will be required prior to any PHI processing.
- Questionnaire: CAIQ is preferred for speed, but we can accept a SIG prefill if it’s available. Please indicate which you’ll start with.
- KMS/BYOK: We prefer BYOK for EU tenants. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys (BYOK) or HSM integrations?

Procurement notes: we have a two-week internal window for initial legal review; any delays on evidence could push our pilot timeline. Point-of-contact for evidence is myself (e.cruz@aurorafin.com) and Lisa Hu (security@aurorafin.com).

Elena
Senior Product Ops, AuroraFin

Hi Elena — thanks for the fast responses and for the scope spreadsheet. A few clarifying points and what we will provide next: 

Clarifying questions:
- For EU residency: can you confirm whether AuroraFin requires physical separation (EU-only tenancy) or just data-at-rest in EU regions for certain customers? That affects our deployment recommendation.
- HIPAA: can you indicate expected volume (number of records/day) and whether AuroraFin will sign a BAA prior to pilot or only at production?

What Redwood will prepare (target delivery Nov 10):
- SOC 2: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary + attestation date) and a timeframe for full report delivery.
- CAIQ prefill: we’ll start with the CAIQ and mark any fields that need customer-specific evidence. If you prefer SIG instead we can convert but CAIQ is typically faster for initial reviews.
- KMS/BYOK doc: short note on our supported key-management patterns (we support KMS integrations and a BYOK path for Dedicated/private deployments — details in the KMS doc).
- Network & app diagram: high-level architecture diagram (no secrets).

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood will create a shared Drive folder and upload the SOC 2 summary, CAIQ draft, and KMS note — link below.
2) Schedule a 30-minute security-to-security prefill call: I can do Nov 10 at 10:00 AM PT or Nov 11 at 9:00 AM PT — please confirm which works for Lisa/your team.
3) AuroraFin: if you can complete column B (tenant & data residency rows) in aurorafin_sig_scope.xlsx by Nov 12, that will let us mark CAIQ fields as satisfied or flagged.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwood-AuroraFin-SIG
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/AF-5921

If that timeline works I’ll open the CAIQ prefill and tag the fields we expect AuroraFin to own.

Thanks — Grace
Security Programs Manager, Redwood Inference
